JOOL SUITES.note: Freehold boutique block of 52 units at 2 Sing Joo Walk (TOP 2014), dominated by shoebox 1-bedders of 387–484 sqft plus small 2-bedders and penthouses, with only basic facilities (pool, gym, BBQ). Walking distance to Farrer Park MRT (NE8) with Boon Keng (NE9) nearby; no collective sale attempt is on record for the development.

SELETAR PARK RESIDENCE.note: 99-year leasehold, 276 units across three 5-storey blocks at 17–21 Seletar Road, developed by Asplenium Land with TOP in 2015. Stacked Homes' analysis flags it as an underperformer at roughly 0.74% annualised return, attributing this to pricing expectations and competition from nearby ECs, and it has no MRT within walking distance (Ang Mo Kio is about a 5-minute drive).

ICON.note: 99-year leasehold 46-storey tower of 646 mostly 1- and 2-bedroom units at 10 Gopeng Street, completed 2007, making it a compact CBD rental play rather than a family product. It sits about 180m from Tanjong Pagar MRT (EWL) and roughly 500m from Maxwell MRT on the Thomson-East Coast Line.

ALEXIS.note: Freehold mixed development of 293 units at 356 Alexandra Road (TOP 2012) with a retail podium below and a 75m sky pool, weighted toward small and studio-type layouts. It is within walking distance of Queenstown MRT (EWL) and next to the Alexandra/Queensway retail belt (IKEA, Queensway Shopping Centre, Anchorpoint), with freehold tenure being its main scarcity argument in District 3.

ONE-NORTH RESIDENCES.note: 99-year leasehold, 405 units at 7 One-North Gateway (TOP 2009), developed by Vista Development, a UOL–Kheng Leong joint venture, and directly served by one-north MRT (CC23) with Buona Vista (CC22/EW21) nearby. Competing new supply has arrived in the same precinct: Hudson Place Residences at Media Circle previewed 1 May 2026 and sold 201 of 327 units on launch weekend at about $2,458 psf average.

THE COAST AT SENTOSA COVE.note: 99-year leasehold waterfront project in Sentosa Cove developed by Ho Bee Land, currently listed in the S$3.1m–S$15.3m range at roughly S$1,464–S$3,202 psf, a wide spread reflecting thin, unit-specific transaction volume. The key demand constraint is unchanged: foreign buyers of non-landed homes face 60% ABSD, and Sentosa Cove condo transaction volumes have been well below the enclave's peak years.

THE BERTH BY THE COVE.note: The 200-unit Berth by the Cove was the first condominium to debut in Sentosa Cove, developed by Ho Bee Land on a 99-year lease from March 2004 (about 77 years remaining) and completed in 2006. At its November 2004 launch roughly 97 units sold at a median of $847 psf, so long-held units have a very low cost base but face the same 60% foreigner ABSD constraint on exit.

THE WOODGROVE.note: Small 99-year leasehold development of 72 units at 3 Woodgrove Drive by Heeton Estate, completed in 1998, so lease decay is now the dominant pricing factor; transactions over the past 12 months ranged S$937–S$1,038 psf, averaging about S$985 psf. Nearest stations are Marsiling (NS8) and Woodlands (NS9/TE2), and the Johor Bahru–Singapore RTS Link terminating at Woodlands North is targeted to begin passenger service around end-2026, alongside the ongoing Woodlands Regional Centre build-out.

GUILLEMARD EDGE.note: Freehold, 275 units over 8 floors at 38 Lorong 30 Geylang by Macly Equity (TOP 2015), transacting at roughly S$1,103–S$1,814 psf over the past 12 months with an average near S$1,627 psf. It is walkable to Dakota, Aljunied and Mountbatten MRT stations, and the announced relocation of Paya Lebar Air Base is the main long-dated catalyst for the wider Geylang/Guillemard belt.

BLUE HORIZON.note: Large 616-unit development at 21–31 West Coast Crescent on a 99-year lease from 2000 (about 74 years remaining), completed 2005, mostly 2- and 3-bedroom stock; no collective sale is on record. Cross Island Line Phase 2 is under construction with the new West Coast (CR18) and Clementi (CR17) stations targeted for completion in 2032, which is the main connectivity upgrade for this pocket.
